name: Dale Hamm
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember loading stock bought with a domestic mortgage.” People around the brick passage off the shop row know Dale by a small Saturday habit. Dale takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I bought supplies for the new business. My own small mortgage now depends on that family's next argument.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. Dale has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Dale looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
personality: Dale keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Dale wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To receive payment for stock without pressuring the guarantor.
family: Finn Ryan is Dale’s second cousin. Dale is free to hang up first. Finn makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The carer's afternoon*, Finn says, “I work the night before. I can do tea but nobody should ask me to drive.”
connections: Parker Osborne. A supplier's small mortgage explains why a carefully recorded old debt is worth studying.

reactions.situation: A borrower learns exactly what the guarantee cost
reactions.response: Dale puts the actual pledged property and repayment date on paper.

reactions.response: Dale asks them privately what can be shared about the delay and respects the answer.
